papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of patients with diminished ovarian reserve regarding traditional Chinese medicine treatment: structural equation modelling analysis.
papers.authors: Jiang F, Zheng J, Su L, Cai J, Hong J
papers.abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of patients with diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) regarding Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatments. A cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2023 to August 2024 among patients with DOR to assess their KAP regarding TCM treatments. Data on characteristics and KAP scores were collected via a self-designed questionnaire. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was employed to assess the relationships among the KAP dimensions. A total of 439 valid responses from patients with DOR were included in the final analysis (effective response rate 82.2%). Patients with DOR had a moderate level of knowledge (median [IQR]: 7.00 [5.00-8.00]), generally positive attitudes (median [IQR]: 27.00 [25.00-28.00]), and suboptimal practices (median [IQR]: 31.00 [28.00-33.00]). SEM showed that knowledge had a direct effect on attitude (β = 0.183, P < 0.001) and practice (β = 0.199, P < 0.001), attitude had a direct effect on practice (β = 0.267, P < 0.001), and knowledge indirectly affected practice through attitude (β = 0.049, P = 0.001). Patients with DOR had inadequate TCM knowledge but positive attitudes. Low practice engagement highlights a need for better education to convert attitudes into effective TCM use for managing ovarian decline.

papers.title: Gut microbiome intervention in gut-brain axis and effects on vascular dementia with prospects on non-pharmacological intervention.
papers.authors: Maurya Y, George EA, Roy A, Menon GJ, Harshitha KR, Priyadharshini K et al.
papers.abstract: Vascular dementia (VD) is the second leading cause of cognitive impairment after Alzheimer's disease. Current treatments focus primarily on managing vascular risk factors with no effective interventions for repairing existing brain damage. Recent research underscores a critical link between gut microbiota and brain function through immunological, hormonal and metabolic pathways. Alterations in the gut microbiome influence vascular cognitive impairment via mechanisms such as dysbiosis, induced intestinal permeability, systemic inflammation, oxidative stress and blood-brain barrier disruption. Microbial metabolites including butyrate promote neuroprotection and maintain vascular integrity, whereas trimethylamine N-oxide is associated with vascular injury and cognitive decline. Restoration of microbial balance through probiotics, plant-based bioactive compounds and traditional medicines has shown potential in preclinical models for regulating inflammation, improving cognitive outcomes though clinical validation is limited. Non-pharmacological approaches like electro-acupuncture further modulate the microbiome and serotonin regulation. This review explores how changes in gut microbiome influence vascular cognitive impairment and discusses therapeutic strategies for restoring microbial balance. Integrating contemporary and traditional strategies, gut microbiome modulation emerges as a potential therapeutic target for the prevention and management of VD although its clinical applicability remains to be fully established.

papers.title: Integrating at-line nanofractionation platform with GNPS for unveiling neuraminidase inhibitors from ethanolic extract of Smilax china L.
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.authors: Chen Z, Xu S, Cassas F, Xu L, Wang J, Pang M et al.
papers.abstract: Influenza is a highly transmissible airborne disease that causes acute febrile respiratory illness, ranging from mild fatigue to fatal respiratory failure. Neuraminidase (NA) serves as a primary drug target for both the prevention and treatment of influenza. In this study, an efficient strategy integrating an at-line nanofractionation (ANF) platform with Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking (GNPS) was employed for the rapid discovery of neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) from the Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) Smilax china L. High-throughput screening of a self-constructed TCM extract library revealed that the ethanolic extract of Smilax china L. exhibited over 90% inhibitory activity against oseltamivir-sensitive neuraminidase (NAS), with an IC50 value of 88.78 ± 13.26 μg/mL. The NAS-based ANF platform was then applied, and 21 compounds were prioritized as candidate NAIs based on their association with bioactive ANF fractions. By combining GNPS molecular networking with manual interpretation (mass errors <5 ppm), a total of 97 compounds were annotated (Confidence level II), covering six major classes, including 47 flavonoids, 20 cinnamic acid derivatives, 16 polyphenolic compounds, and 14 others. Among these, the 21 bioactive constituents included chlorogenic acid, astilbin, procyanidin B, and smilaside A. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to explore potential binding interactions and possible structural determinants of candidate binding. The results suggest that these compounds may interact with key residues in the NAS active site, including the 150-loop, the Arg cluster (residues 118, 292, 371), and Glu119. Notably, the 150-loop region is relatively conserved, suggesting a potential structural basis for hypothesizing activity against drug-resistant variants that warrants further experimental investigation. However, docking scores and MD stability are computational predictions and do not establish experimental inhibitory potency; biochemical and antiviral validation is required. The integrated ANF-GNPS platform established in this study provides an efficient and reliable technical approach for the rapid screening and structural annotation of bioactive constituents from TCM. It lays a solid chemical foundation for the discovery of novel NAIs.

papers.title: An integrated FIDI-MS and UPLC-Q-TOF/MS strategy for rapid functional screening and chemical characterization of antioxidants in Polygonum multiflorum.
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.authors: Xu M, Ma Z, Liu J, Wang L, Ocholi SS, Zhang Z et al.
papers.abstract: A novel integrated strategy combining field-induced droplet ionization mass spectrometry (FIDI-MS) with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF/MS) was developed for the rapid screening and identification of antioxidant constituents in herbal extracts. This approach enables real-time assessment of antioxidant activity within microdroplets and comprehensive compositional characterization of complex matrices. Applied to Polygonum multiflorum extract (PME), the method successfully identified known antioxidants such as 2,3,5,4'-tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucoside (TSG) and revealed additional bioactive phytochemicals. Quantitative FIDI-MS dose-response profiling determined the antioxidant potency of key compounds, with trans-TSG exhibiting superior activity (IC50 = 13.33 ± 1.06 μM) compared to its cis-isomer and emodin. By integrating functional screening, reliable chemical profiling, and targeted quantification, the strategy enabled comprehensive analysis of bioactive constituents in complex herbal samples. Furthermore, the utility of FIDI-MS, when coupled with chromatographic separation and high-resolution mass detection, is underscored as a complementary approach for functional and chemical interrogation of bioactive compounds in botanical matrices.

papers.title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial.
papers.authors: Sim J, Choi KS, Lee DH
papers.abstract:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by restricted and repetitive behaviors and disturbances in social communication and interaction. Currently, there is no fundamental treatment for ASD, with only a few medications available for use on a limited basis to manage concomitant neuropsychiatric symptoms. The primary therapeutic goal of such treatments is to alleviate symptoms while maximizing the functional independence and quality of life of affected individuals. Many complementary and alternative medicine therapies have been reported to have effects on ASD symptoms; however, evidence is insufficient to confirm their clinical effectiveness. Acupuncture has traditionally been used as a complementary intervention to manage various neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including ASD, in East Asia. However, how acupuncture stimulation modulates neural activity at the macroscale level in individuals with ASD remains largely unknown.
This study aims to elucidate disease-related brain alterations and explore the acute neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD and in typically developing (TD) individuals, using a multimodal neuroimaging approach.
This study was designed as a randomized, sham-controlled trial. In this stratified 2×2 design, 70 participants, including individuals with ASD (n=35) and TD controls (n=35), will each be randomly assigned to either the verum or sham acupuncture group, resulting in 4 groups. The verum acupuncture group will receive stimulation at specific acupoints clinically indicated for ASD, eliciting a deqi sensation. The sham acupuncture group will receive superficial needling at nonacupoints unrelated to ASD symptoms. Each group will undergo clinical assessments and multimodal neuroimaging measurements, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy and electroencephalography, before and after acupuncture stimulation. The primary outcome will be differences in resting state network metrics and relative band power in frontal areas by disease status. Secondary outcomes will include differences in these neural markers following acupuncture stimulation between the verum and sham groups, reflecting the group × intervention interaction. Exploratory outcomes will focus on identifying neural markers that correlate with clinical indicators of ASD.
Recruitment began in April 2025. To date, 23 individuals with ASD and 21 TD individuals have participated in this study. The recruitment process is expected to continue until December 2026.
ASD presents a significant socioeconomic burden, with no definitive treatment established to date. Although acupuncture is a widely applied intervention for various neurological conditions, including ASD, its large-scale neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.

papers.title: TRDMT1-dependent m5C modification of TLR4 mediates the protective effects of Shaoyao decoction in TNBS-induced Crohn's disease.
papers.authors: Deng Y, Wang J, Li M, Xiao G, Pan Y, Tao Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the digestive system with increasing morbidity worldwide. Shaoyao Decoction (SYD), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, has shown therapeutic potential in the treatment of CD. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the protective effects of SYD against 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced CD-like colitis through the tRNA aspartic acid methyltransferase 1 (TRDMT1)/TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.
We used network pharmacology to identify potential targets and related pathways of SYD in the treatment of CD. The CD model was induced by TNBS. Immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and ELISA were employed to detect various cytokines and proteins associated with epithelial barrier, inflammation, apoptosis, and signaling pathway regulation. TLR4 mRNA expression and the 5-methylcytosine (m5C) modification level of TLR4 mRNA were assayed by qRT-PCR and MeRIP-qPCR. TRDMT1 silencing in Caco2 cells and TLR4 knockout (TLR4-/-) mice were used to verify the mechanism by which SYD attenuated CD symptoms.
The TLR4/NF-κB pathway was identified as the core regulatory mechanism. Administration of SYD alleviated TNBS-induced CD-like colitis in mice, as evidenced by the restoration of intestinal mucosal barrier integrity, reduced inflammation, and decreased apoptosis. At the molecular level, SYD reduced the expression of TLR4 and MyD88, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, and increased TRDMT1 expression. SYD also enhanced the m5C modification level of TLR4 mRNA. Furthermore, mechanistic studies indicated that TRDMT1 and TLR4 were involved in the protective effects of SYD against CD-like colitis.
SYD can alleviate intestinal inflammation, inhibit apoptosis, and protect the intestinal barrier in the CD model. This protective effect may be mediated through upregulation of TRDMT1, which enhances the m5C modification of TLR4 mRNA, thereby reducing TLR4 expression and suppressing TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling.

papers.title: Salvianolic acid a alleviates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats via SIRT1-mediated inhibition of oxidative stress and inflammation.
papers.authors: Chen Z, Cao Y, Bo H, Yang Y, Liu D, Mao C et al.
papers.abstract:
Salvia miltiorrhiza (SM) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and salvianolic acid A (SAA) is its main bioactive component. Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is common in ischemic heart disease treatment, mainly caused by inflammation and oxidative stress.
To clarify the role of SIRT1 (Sirtuin 1) in SAA's protection against MIRI and the underlying signaling pathways.
The potential targets of SAA and MIRI were identified using SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, TargetNet, GeneCards, OMIM and CTD databases. Gene Ontology Enrichment (GO) and Signaling Pathway Enrichment (KEGG) analyses were performed on these targets. Molecular docking examined SIRT1-SAA interactions. In vivo MIRI models were established by left anterior descending coronary artery ligation in rats, while H9c2 cell hypoxia-reoxygenation (H/R) models served for in vitro studies. Western blotting (WB), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay, immunofluorescence (IF) staining and Quantitative reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were employed to validate the effects of SAA on MIRI therapy. SIRT1 siRNA knockdown confirmed its regulatory role in SAA's antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions against MIRI.
SAA alleviated MIRI dose-dependently by inhibiting inflammation and oxidative stress, with high binding affinity to SIRT1 (molecular docking). SAA upregulated SIRT1 expression and exerted antiapoptotic effects, activating the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) pathway and suppressing the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathway via SIRT1.
SAA mitigates MIRI-induced oxidative stress and inflammation by activating SIRT1, which regulates the PGC-1α/Nrf2/HO-1 and NF-κB pathways. This confirms SIRT1 as the key upstream mediator of SAA's cardioprotective effects, supporting SAA as a potential therapeutic agent for MIRI.

papers.title: Multi-omics reveals that burdock seed aglycone alleviates renal fibrosis by restoring mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation function.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Wu G, Zhao L, Bo Y, Yang D, Guo J et al.
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis (RF), a common pathological process driving chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression to end-stage renal failure, is closely associated with oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Arctigenin (ATG), the main active component of burdock seed, exhibits anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic activities, but its mechanisms in RF treatment remain unclear. Here, we performed integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses to identify key targets and pathways of ATG in a unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced rat RF model. Multi-omics enrichment analysis revealed that NDUFS8 and NDUFS2 were the core targets of ATG, with the OXPHOS pathway as the central intersecting pathway. Our results suggest that ATG exerts anti-renal fibrosis effects by targeting the OXPHOS pathway to inhibit excessive reactive oxygen species production and oxidative stress. SIGNIFICANCE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) continues to impose an escalating global health and socioeconomic burden, while renal fibrosis (RF), as the convergent pathological endpoint of virtually all progressive nephropathies, remains the principal determinant of irreversible renal failure and adverse clinical outcomes. Despite extensive efforts to develop antifibrotic therapies, effective clinical interventions remain elusive, largely due to the complex and multifactorial nature of RF pathogenesis. In this study, we employed an integrated multi-omics framework encompassing transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics to systematically decipher the antifibrotic mechanism of arctigenin (ATG), a bioactive natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine. Our findings identify mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation as the pivotal regulatory axis underlying the renoprotective effects of ATG and further establish key catalytic subunits of mitochondrial complex I as its direct molecular targets. Mechanistically, ATG not only restores complex I activity and reprograms mitochondrial energy metabolism but also preserves the intracellular stability and localization of these subunits, thereby preventing their aberrant release-mediated inflammatory activation and disrupting the self-perpetuating cycle linking metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and fibrosis progression. Beyond revealing a previously unrecognized dual mechanism integrating metabolic and inflammatory regulation, this study provides compelling evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction is not merely a secondary consequence of tissue injury but a fundamental driver of fibrotic remodeling. Importantly, our work highlights the translational potential of natural product-based mitochondrial interventions for CKD treatment and supports a broader conceptual shift toward metabolism-centered therapeutic strategies for chronic fibrotic diseases. Given the central role of mitochondrial dysfunction across multiple organs, these findings may also have far-reaching implications for the treatment of systemic fibrosis-related disorders beyond the kidney.

papers.title: Identification of anti-NSCLC bioactive compounds from Euphorbia helioscopia L. through integrated pharmacological classification and metabolomics analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
papers.authors: Yu X, Bai C, Wang T, Yang Y, Deng Y, Li C et al.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia helioscopia L. (commonly known as Zeqi) has been reported to possess anti-tumor potential, however, its bioactive constituents and underlying molecular mechanisms against non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain to be elucidated. This study aimed to systematically identify anti-NSCLC components and explore their associated mechanisms through integrated pharmacological classification and metabolomics analysis. Zeqi samples exhibiting distinct in vitro antiproliferative activities were first classified into relatively higher-activity (RHA) and relatively lower-activity (RLA) group, and then subjected to metabolomics profiling using ultra performance liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (UPLC-HRMS) and subsequent univariate and multivariate statistical analysis. Four compounds (fraxetin, 2''-O-galloylhyperoside, isofraxidin and myricitrin 3-O-galactoside) were identified as candidate bioactive constituents associated with the antiproliferative activity of Zeqi. Among these, fraxetin exhibited the most potent inhibitory effect against NSCLC cells. Flow cytometric analysis revealed a dose-dependent increase in apoptotic rates. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that fraxetin regulates the expression of apoptosis-related genes and activates apoptotic pathways. Further reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blot analyses confirmed that fraxetin-induced apoptosis in NSCLC cells might be associated with its ability to upregulate Noxa and downregulate Mcl-1 at both transcriptional and translational levels. In conclusion, the successful application of integrated pharmacological classification and metabolomics analysis not only enabled the identification of anti-NSCLC active components in Zeqi but also provides a robust methodological framework for efficient discovery of bioactive lead compounds from complex traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) systems.

papers.title: Integration of multidimensional data acquisition and data processing strategy for comprehensive characterization of chemical constituents in Qingre Sanjie capsule by UPLC-TWIMS-QTOF-MS and molecular networking.
papers.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
papers.authors: Zhang S, Ma S, Chen X, Hu R, Zhang J, Zhao Y et al.
papers.abstract: Molecular networking (MN) is widely utilized in the compositional analysis of herbal medicines and complex formulations. While the technique effectively links compounds through shared MS2 fragmentation patterns and structural homology, it is often compromised by dispersed in-source fragment ions and adduct ions, which weaken spectral correlations and introduce redundant nodes. To address these limitations, we propose a novel integrated strategy combining Ion Identity Molecular Networking (IIMN) and Feature-Based Molecular Networking (FBMN), aiming to reduce interference from co-eluted ions and to enhance isomers discrimination, respectively. Evaluation based on precursor ion node counts, edge connectivity, and cluster topology confirmed IIMN and FBMN as complementary methods for identifying non-isomers and isomers, respectively. Importantly, IIMN significantly strengthens network connectivity, reduces data redundancy, and improves annotation reliability across diverse ion species. To demonstrate the applicability of this strategy, we employed Qingre Sanjie Capsule (QSC), a traditional Chinese medicine prescription for treating upper respiratory tract infections and allergic conjunctivitis, as a case study and performed systematic chemical identification using ultra-high performance liquid chromatography coupled with traveling wave ion mobility quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-TWIMS-QTOF-MS). Two hybrid scan modes, Data-Dependent Acquisition (DDA) and high-definition DDA, were utilized to acquire both precursor and fragment ion data. A total of 143 compounds were unambiguously identified or tentatively characterized, including three novel constituents first reported. This strategy effectively minimizes interference from redundant nodes, increases the capacity for novel compound discovery, and provides a valuable approach for the systematic analysis of complex systems.

papers.title: Rapid evaluation and mechanistic study of the whitening activity of dandelion extract based on UV-Vis spectroscopy.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Chen T, Tang X, Wei Z, Xu J, Huang G, Meng H et al.
papers.abstract: To enable rapid prediction of the skin-whitening efficacy of dandelion ethanol extract, quantitative prediction models for ABTS and DPPH radical scavenging activities, tyrosinase inhibition rate, and whitening activity index were developed using ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy combined with chemometric methods. The underlying mechanisms were further investigated through Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and molecular docking studies. The results demonstrated that UV-Vis spectroscopy combined with feature extraction exhibited robust predictive performance for all whitening-related indicators. The optimal prediction correlation coefficients (Rp2) for each indicator exceeded 0.85, and the residual predictive deviation (RPD) values in the validation set were greater than 2.5. Compared to raw spectra, the application of feature extraction could significantly enhance the performance of predictive models. The functional group information obtained from FT-IR, characteristic ultraviolet absorption wavelengths, and LC-MS/MS analysis collectively indicated that flavonoids and phenolic acids were the primary active components contributing to the whitening efficacy. Molecular docking analysis revealed that flavonoids and phenolic acids exhibited stable binding interactions with key target proteins, indicating their potential role in inhibiting melanin synthesis and contributing to the whitening efficacy. This study presented a rapid and reliable approach for evaluating the whitening activity of dandelion ethanol extract. Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms were elucidated through an integrated analysis combining spectroscopic characterization, component identification, and molecular mechanisms. These findings could provide methodological support for the efficient evaluation of whitening efficacy in traditional Chinese medicine and contribute to a deeper understanding of its mechanistic basis.

papers.title: 3D magnetic nanocomposite modified with molybdenum disulfide: preparation and application in aqueous Cr(vi) remediation.
papers.authors: Duan X, Zhang J, Wang Y, Miao B, Yu Y, Guo S et al.
papers.abstract: Hexavalent chromium (Cr(vi)) poses severe environmental risks due to its high toxicity, persistence, and bioaccumulation. Adsorption technology is recognized as one of the core strategies for Cr(vi) remediation, but the development of low-cost, high-efficiency biochar-based adsorbents remains an urgent demand. In this work, 3D Molybdenum disulfide Magnetic Biochar (3DMMB) was successfully fabricated via a combination of calcination pyrolysis and hydrothermal methods, using traditional Chinese medicine residues (CMR) as the biomass feedstock and iron-based sludge (IS) as an alternative to conventional iron sources. Solution pH was found to exert a significant influence on Cr(vi) removal, with an acidic environment being favorable for Cr(vi) adsorption. Kinetic and isothermal analyses revealed that the adsorption process fits well with the pseudo-second-order kinetic model and Langmuir isotherm model, confirming that the adsorption is an endothermic and spontaneous monolayer process, dominated by chemical adsorption as the rate-limiting step, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 83.33 mg g-1. The potential adsorption mechanisms mainly involve physical adsorption, electrostatic interaction, chemical reduction, and complexation. Notably, 3DMMB exhibits excellent recyclability and regeneration performance, retaining 89.55% of its initial adsorption capacity after six cycles of desorption and regeneration. This study provides a novel and cost-effective approach for the preparation of waste-derived functional adsorbents and realizes selective and efficient purification of Cr(vi)-contaminated wastewater through sulfur-based grafting modification.

papers.title: Metabolic-Epigenetic Reprogramming of Fibroblast-Like Synoviocytes in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Perspectives for Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Han K
papers.abstract:
In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), persistent synovial inflammation and clinical relapse cannot be fully explained by immune activation alone, as fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) can acquire stable pathogenic states that sustain synovitis and joint destruction. Metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodeling are functionally integrated in RA-FLS, thereby promoting hyperproliferation, invasiveness, apoptosis resistance, and inflammatory memory.
In this review, we summarize the interplay between altered cellular metabolism and epigeneticmechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, RNA modifications, and chromatin remodeling, and discuss how this interplay contributes tostabilizing pathogenic FLS phenotypes.We further discuss gut microbiota-associated metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, tryptophan derivatives, and one-carbon metabolites, as potential mediators linking systemic metabolic imbalance to FLS epigenetic states. These metabolites may act through histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition, modulation of methyl donor availability, and receptor-mediated inflammatory signaling. From the perspective of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), we propose that TCM formulations and bioactive compounds may modulate this network through microbiota-dependent metabolic remodeling and direct suppression of FLS activation. Finally, we identify current evidence gaps and highlight emerging therapeutic strategies, including metabolomics-guided fecal microbiota transplantation and FLS-targeted epigenetic interventions.
This review highlights metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming as a key mechanism underlying persistent RA-FLS phenotypes. Interactions among thegut microbiota, microbial metabolites, and epigenetic regulation provide a promising framework for linking systemic metabolic disturbances to local joint damage. Future studies integrating multi-omics profiling, microbiome modulation, and FLS-targeted epigenetic interventions are needed to clarify causality and facilitate more precise therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Discovery of the mechanism of Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction in the treatment of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy with Qi Deficiency and Blood Stasis based on the dynamic metabolic trajectory analysis.
papers.authors: Wen J, Yan L, Xiang Y, Wang X, Fang C, Ru S et al.
papers.abstract:
Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction (HGWD), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, has shown clinical efficacy in the treatment of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) with Qi deficiency and blood stasis syndrome. However, its pharmacodynamic material basis and underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to systematically elucidate the pharmacodynamic material basis and therapeutic mechanisms of HGWD in the treatment of DPN using an integrated Chinmedomics strategy.
A rat model of DPN with Qi deficiency and blood stasis syndrome was established by streptozotocin (STZ) injection combined with dietary intervention and exhaustive swimming. HGWD was administered continuously for 8 weeks to assess its therapeutic effects. In addition to conventional pharmacological assessments, ANOVA-simultaneous component analysis (ASCA) was applied to urinary metabolomics analysis to dynamically track metabolic trajectories and characterize time-dependent changes in disease-related urinary biomarkers. Blood-absorbed components in the HGWD-treated group were characterized using UHPLC-QE-Orbitrap-MS. Correlation analysis was then performed among urinary biomarkers, key pharmacodynamic indicators, and in vivo active components. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro experiments were further conducted to validate the core active components and their corresponding targets.
HGWD significantly improved neurological function and alleviated pathological damage in the DPN rat model. Urinary metabolomics analysis identified 28 disease-related urinary biomarkers that were markedly modulated by HGWD treatment. Under conditions of confirmed therapeutic efficacy, 98 blood-absorbed components, including 63 prototype compounds and 35 metabolites, were identified. Integrated correlation analysis and network pharmacology revealed eight key pharmacodynamic components and three core targets closely associated with the therapeutic effects of HGWD. Among these components, astragaloside II, paeoniflorin, and quercetin were identified as major bioactive compounds, which may exert therapeutic effects by regulating the protein expression of P-gp, PTP1B, and MMP2.
This study systematically clarified the pharmacodynamic material basis and therapeutic mechanisms of HGWD in the treatment of DPN using an integrated Chinmedomics approach. The integrated analysis identified 17 urinary biomarkers, 8 core components, and 3 core targets, namely ABCB1, MMP2, and PTPN1, which were further supported by molecular simulations and in vitro validation These findings provide a comprehensive strategy for deciphering the mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine formulas and support the potential application of HGWD in DPN treatment.

papers.title: Agriophyllum squarrosum oligosaccharides ameliorate inflammation and lipid accumulation in T2DM-induced MASLD via miR-155-regulated PPARγ signaling pathways.
papers.authors: Bao S, Lin M, Wang X, Wu Q, Yin J, Wu R et al.
papers.abstract:
Agriophyllum squarrosum (L.) Moq., is a traditional medicinal herb first recorded in the "Four Medical Tantras" during the 8th century AD. It is commonly employed in Mongolian medicine for various therapeutic diseases, including the dispelling epidemics, heat clearance, detoxification, and diuresis. This herb is known to inhibit "He Yi," regulate "Ba Da Gan," and is utilized in the treatment of "Xi He Ri Xi Jing Bing" which corresponds to modern diabetes and xiaoke in traditional Chinese medicine. Agriophyllum squarrosum oligosaccharides (AOS) are recognized as major bioactive constituents, however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)-related metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear.
This study investigates the therapeutic effects of AOS in T2DM-MASLD and explores the underlying mechanisms involving miR-155-mediated signaling pathways.
In vivo, db/db mice were treated with AOS, and hepatic lipid accumulation and insulin resistance were evaluated using biochemical and histological analyses. Hepatic expression of miR-155 and associated signaling proteins was observed by qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Exosomes derived from ATMs of db/db mice were co-cultured with AML-12 hepatocytes to investigate the role of exosomal miR-155 in MASLD progression. In vitro, inflammatory cytokine production and miR-155 expression were quantified using ELISA and qRT-PCR, while exosomal miR-155 secretion was evaluated in glucolipid-induced cellular injury models.
AOS treatment reduced hepatic steatosis and improved insulin resistance in db/db mice. AOS was associated with decreased hepatic miR-155 expression. Exosomal miR-155 derived from ATMs aggravated hepatocyte injury in the co-culture system, accompanied by increased expression of SREBP1c, NLRP3, and NF-κB p65. In vitro, AOS inhibited exosomal miR-155 secretion and downregulated the expression of SREBP1c, P2X7R, NF-κB p65, and inhibitor of IκBα, thus attenuating glucolipid metabolism-associated inflammatory responses and lipid dysregulation.
AOS ameliorates inflammation, hepatic lipid accumulation, and insulin resistance in T2DM-associated MASLD, possibly via suppression of miR-155 and modulation of downstream inflammatory and lipogenic signaling pathways. These results identify AOS as a promising therapeutic candidate for treating T2DM-associated MASLD.

papers.title: The History of Chinese Pathology: Ancient and Imperial China.
papers.journal: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
papers.authors: Shen S, Lu W, Huang S, Ding Y, Bian X
papers.abstract: Humans have long sought to comprehend the etiology and mechanisms of disease, as well as the pathological alterations underlying clinical manifestations at the onset of illness. In ancient Chinese myths and legends, disease was commonly attributed to supernatural forces such as demons and malevolent spirits. With a better understanding of the natural world, these early superstitions gave way to explanations based on natural causation. Around the time that Hippocrates advanced the concept that natural factors were important in health and disease, Chinese medical scholars developed the theoretical framework of Yin-Yang and the Five Elements to explain the origins and progression of disease. Over time, theories of disease evolved, due to transformations in religion, philosophy, science, and technology. The study of disease transitioned from rudimentary and speculative accounts to systematic investigations encompassing organs, tissues, and cells. When missionaries introduced Western medicine to China, it was gradually gained acceptance among part of the medical community. In China today, both Western medicine and traditional Chinese medicine are actively supported and seen as complementary approaches to health care. The rich history of Chinese pathology is not well documented in Western medical literature. In this review, we explain the key theories, events, practitioners, and scholars in Chinese pathology, covering ancient China (before 221 bce) to the end of Imperial China (1912 ce).

papers.title: Program Evaluation of Acupuncture and Massage Services Delivered for Symptom Management at a Community Cancer Clinic.
papers.authors: Booher AG, Rico C, Nouvini R, Killoran K, Drullinsky P, Maxwell S et al.
papers.abstract:
High symptom burden disproportionately affects minoritized racial and ethnic groups during cancer treatments and exacerbates health disparities related to quality of life, treatment adherence, and overall survival. Acupuncture and massage have a growing evidence base for cancer symptom management, as shown in recent guidelines from ASCO and the Society for Integrative Oncology. However, access remains limited in community-based, underserved settings.
We conducted a program evaluation of integrative medicine services at a community cancer clinic in East Harlem, New York. Auricular acupuncture and massage were offered 1 day a week to patients with cancer in the chemoinfusion suites at no additional cost. We collected demographics and clinical characteristics of patient visits, as well as types of treatments delivered and reasons treatments were not received. We assessed pain, fatigue, anxiety, and nausea immediately pre- and post-treatment, as well as patient satisfaction.
From 2022 to 2024, we offered acupuncture or massage at 635 patient visits, which were predominantly non-White (82.4%), Hispanic (44.9%), Spanish-speaking (31.7%), and Medicaid-insured (45.5%). Of these 635 patient visits, 396 (62.4%) received acupuncture or massage. Of the 239 who did not receive treatment, the most common reasons were lack of time (54.4%) and lack of interest (38.9%). Rates of treatment receipt were higher among female, Hispanic, Spanish-speaking, Medicare-insured, and chemotherapy patient visits (all P < .05). Patients reported reductions in pain, fatigue, anxiety, and nausea immediately post-treatment. More than 90% of treatment recipients reported satisfaction with the program.
This program reached a diverse, underserved population with historically limited access to integrative therapies. The findings highlight the barriers and facilitators to bringing acupuncture and massage services to community-based oncology settings.

papers.title: Analysis of Acupoint Selection and Combinations in Acupuncture Treatment of Endometriosis: A Protocol for Data Mining.
papers.authors: Dai L, Zhang Y, Wang L
papers.abstract:
Endometriosis, characterized by dysmenorrhea and pelvic pain, is a common gynecological disease. Acupuncture, as a complementary and alternative therapy for endometriosis, has been supported by a large body of clinical evidence. However, due to the heterogeneity of acupoint prescriptions, the commonly used acupoints remain undetermined.
This study aims to identify the commonly used acupoint selection and combination patterns for the treatment of endometriosis through a comprehensive data mining analysis based on existing literature.
We will systematically search 8 databases (Web of Science (WOS), PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Wanfang, Chongqing VIP database, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database (CBM)) from their inception to September 30, 2026. Only acupuncture clinical trials will be included. All other types will be excluded. Literature deduplication will be performed using NoteExpress 4.3. Data management and descriptive statistical analysis will be completed using WPS Spreadsheets (version 12.1.0.26375). Association rule analysis will be conducted in SPSS Modeler 14.1. Cluster analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and decision tree analysis will be implemented using SPSS Statistics 26.0.
Our study will conduct an in-depth exploration of the frequently uesd acupoint selection and combination patterns for treating patients with endometriosis.
The findings of this study will identify commonly used acupoints and potentially relevant acupoint combinations for acupuncture treatment in patients with endometriosis, and provide a basis for subsequent clinical decision-making, and for the selection of acupoints in prospective randomized controlled trials, thereby helping both clinicians and patients make more informed choices.

papers.title: Adjunctive Acorus tatarinowii essential-oil ear-canal packing for idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss: study protocol for a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
papers.authors: Chen S, Xu H, He X, Tang X
papers.abstract:
Idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL) is an acute otologic emergency, and hearing recovery remains highly variable and frequently unsatisfactory. Acorus tatarinowii Schott has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine to treat hearing impairment and related auditory disorders. Its essential oil (SCP-oil) has demonstrated anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective activities in preclinical studies. Advances in local otologic drug-delivery strategies suggest that administration through the external auditory canal may offer a practical, noninvasive approach to local treatment. This study therefore aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive SCP-oil ear-canal packing in patients with ISSNHL.
This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to be conducted at Zhejiang Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine. The trial has been registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR2026000919). A total of 258 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive conventional therapy combined with either SCP-oil ear-canal packing or glycerin placebo ear-canal packing for 14 consecutive days. The primary outcome is the study-defined total markedly effective rate of hearing recovery at week 2, defined as the proportion of participants achieving complete recovery or marked improvement, as assessed by pure-tone audiometry. Secondary outcomes include the mean improvement in hearing thresholds across the affected frequencies, the hearing-recovery categories, tinnitus severity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), depressive symptoms assessed using the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), and sleep quality assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Efficacy outcomes will be assessed at baseline and week 2, with an additional safety assessment conducted at week 4. Adverse events will be monitored throughout the study.
This trial will provide evidence on the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of adjunctive SCP-oil ear-canal packing for ISSNHL, including its effects on hearing recovery and patient-reported outcomes. The findings may also inform the design of future multicenter clinical trials.

papers.title: Efficacy of acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine, combined acupuncture-herbal therapy, and western medication for adult chronic insomnia: a network meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Yang N, Li Y, Zhao J, Wang R, Wang S, Li Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Chronic insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder that significantly impairs quality of life and reduces patient confidence in treatment. Acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine, and their combination have shown promise in the management of this condition. However, comparative research on these Chinese medicine modalities themselves and vs. Western medication remains scarce.
PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were comprehensively searched from database inception to June 1, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias in the eligible studies. Network meta-analysis was conducted using STATA 16 and R 4.5.3.
Fifty-nine randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 4 interventions were included. According to the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) analysis, for total efficacy (TE), acupuncture plus herbal medicine ranked the highest (92.0%), followed by acupuncture (74.7%), herbal medicine (33.1%), and Western medicine (0.2%). For Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), acupuncture ranked first (82.0%), followed by acupuncture plus herbal medicine (76.8%), herbal medicine (36.4%), and Western medicine (4.9%). For adverse events, where a higher SUCRA indicates fewer events, acupuncture ranked first (78.8%), followed by herbal medicine (76.0%), acupuncture plus herbal medicine (45.2%), and Western medicine (<0.1%).
Combination therapy (acupuncture plus herbal medicine) showed the highest probability of being the most effective intervention for total efficacy based on SUCRA analysis, and significantly outperformed Western medication and herbal medicine alone. However, no significant difference was observed between combination therapy and acupuncture alone. Acupuncture alone ranked first for improving sleep quality (PSQI) and minimizing adverse events. Given the methodological limitations of the included studies, high-quality, rigorously designed RCTs are warranted to validate these findings.

papers.title: Acupuncture is associated with lower accidental injury risk among patients with Parkinson's disease: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Chou HJ, Wang MJ, Lin SK
papers.abstract:
Patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) have a high risk of accidental injuries because motor and non-motor symptoms can impair gait, balance, cognition, and autonomic function. Acupuncture has been reported to improve gait and balance, but its association with long-term injury prevention in PD remains unclear.
We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. Patients newly diagnosed with PD between 2001 and 2012 were followed through 2018. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to improve comparability between patients who received acupuncture and those who did not. The PSM cohort was designated as the primary analysis, and a multivariable analysis of the full cohort was supportive. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
Among 24,467 patients with PD, 7,830 (32.0%) received acupuncture. Accidental injuries occurred in 15.2% of patients in the acupuncture group and 17.1% of patients in the non-acupuncture group. In the primary PSM analysis, acupuncture was associated with a lower risk of hospitalization for accidental injury (aHR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.42-0.85). The association was strongest for accidental falls, although no simple dose-response relationship was observed across acupuncture-session categories. The supportive full-cohort analysis yielded a similar direction of association (aHR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.39-0.76).
In this nationwide claims-based cohort, acupuncture use was associated with a lower risk of hospitalization for accidental injury among patients newly diagnosed with PD. Because residual confounding and differences in care-seeking may remain, prospective studies with clinical measures of PD severity are warranted.

papers.title: Modulating inflammatory cytokines through acupuncture: Evidence from a systematic review.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
papers.authors: Namazi N, Majidi Z, Ghahremani Z, Atlasi R, Liu Q, Kazemi AH
papers.abstract:
Evidence shows the positive effects of acupuncture on the modulation of cytokines. However, findings are conflicting. The present systematic review aimed to clarify the effects of acupuncture on pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines in adults. Five databases, including Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library, were searched without language restrictions until July 1, 2024. Clinical trials that examine the effects of manual acupuncture on at least one of the inflammatory factors (IL-6, TNF-α, or hs-CRP/CRP) in adults, regardless of background disease, were included. Of 12,197 articles, finally 29 were included. All clinical trials examined the effects of acupuncture on both genders aged 21 to 72 years. Duration of the intervention varied between 2 and 12 weeks. The effects of acupuncture on inflammatory and anti-inflammatory parameters were examined on osteoarthritis/ rheumatoid arthritis (n = 8), obesity (n = 4), allergy (n = 4), healthy subjects (n = 3), and Crohn's disease (CD) (n = 2). For several diseases, only one eligible article was found. Risk of bias assessment revealed concerns in all studies across at least three of the six main domains. Acupuncture as an adjuvant therapy is likely modulate cytokine levels in patients with diverse disease backgrounds. Although the positive effects of this type of therapy were reported in most studies, some showed no or even negative effects on cytokine levels. Overall, due to concerns about a high or unclear risk of bias, the findings must be interpreted with great caution. Further high-quality clinical trials are needed to draw definitive conclusions.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02098-w.

papers.title: Gentiopicroside alleviates depression-like symptoms in animal models through regulating COX-2-mediated autophagy and inflammation.
papers.authors: Ke W, Liu G, Lin M, Yao T, He C
papers.abstract: Depression is a serious mental illness affecting millions of people worldwide. This study investigates the effects of gentiopicroside, a compound found in traditional Chinese medicine, on depression-like animal models and its potential mechanism of action. The study utilized rat models with corticosterone-induced depression and treated them with various concentrations of gentiopicroside. The effects on hippocampal cells, serum 5-HT levels, inflammation, autophagy, and oxidative stress markers were observed. The role of Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression and mitophagy was also examined using in vitro neuron cell models. Gentiopicroside demonstrated dose-dependent effects on alleviating hippocampal cell damage, restoring serum 5-HT levels, and inhibiting inflammation and oxidative stress markers. It also promoted autophagy and modulated COX-2 expression in the rat models. The in vitro study revealed that gentiopicroside could regulate COX-2 expression, reduce mitochondrial membrane potential loss and cell apoptosis, and inhibit NLRP3 (NOD-like receptor family, pyrin domain-containing 3) inflammatory complex-related proteins and cytokines. Overexpression of COX-2 significantly reversed the positive effects of gentiopicroside, while PINK1 (PTEN-induced kinase 1) overexpression promoted mitophagy, inhibited NLRP3 inflammatory complex activation, and reduced oxidative stress. Gentiopicroside ameliorates depression-like symptoms in animal models by suppressing COX-2 expression. This suppression is necessary for the subsequent enhancement of PINK1-mediated mitophagy, which helps to re-establish mitochondrial homeostasis and attenuate neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. This novel mechanism may potentially lead to the development of new therapies for depression treatment.

papers.title: Development of a species-specific PCR-lateral flow assay integrated with SYBR Safe for rapid authentication of commercial Polygoni Multiflori Caulis (Ye-Jiao-Teng).
papers.authors: Ngo NP, Kung YY, Chiang P, Lee MS, Chang KW, Wu KC
papers.abstract: Pleuropterus multiflorus (PM) is a widely used medicinal plant in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). However, the closely related species Pleuropterus angulatus (PA) is commonly misidentified as PM due to morphological similarities, leading to frequent adulteration in commercial Polygoni Multiflori Caulis (PMC) products. To address this issue, we developed a species-specific PCR-lateral flow assay integrated with SYBR Safe for rapid and species-specific authentication of PM and PA. Species-specific primers were designed based on a diagnostic single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) within the chloroplast trnL-trnF region. After validation of specificity, visual detection of PM and PA was achieved using lateral flow strips. The assay demonstrated detection limits of 0.5 ng/μL for PM and 0.05 ng/μL for PA genomic DNA. The application of this assay to eighteen commercial PMC products revealed the presence of PA in all samples, with only one product containing both PM and PA, indicating widespread adulteration in the herbal marketplace. In conclusion, the developed PCR-lateral flow assay provides a rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly molecular diagnostic tool suitable for authenticity testing of herbal products and quality control during pharmaceutical manufacturing.

papers.title: Exploration of bioactive natural products from tropical plant genetic resources: from diversity to functional seeds.
papers.authors: Morita H, Hirasawa Y, Kaneda T
papers.abstract: Natural products derived from higher plants continue to represent an important source of structurally diverse and biologically active molecules for drug discovery. In particular, tropical plant genetic resources provide a rich reservoir of unique secondary metabolites owing to their exceptional biodiversity. Through long-term collaborative studies conducted mainly in Southeast Asia, extensive collections of tropical plant materials were screened for diverse biological activities, leading to the discovery of numerous bioactive natural products. Early phytochemical studies on medicinal plants such as Eurycoma longifolia, a well-known traditional herbal medicine widely used in Malaysia and Indonesia, also contributed to the establishment of our research platform for tropical natural product discovery. This review summarizes representative studies on structurally unique compounds isolated from tropical plant resources and highlights their biological activities and mechanisms of action. Representative examples include ceramicines, limonoids from Chisocheton ceramicus with anti-lipid droplet accumulation activity, calofolic acids from Calophyllum scriblitifolium exhibiting vasorelaxant effects through PI3K-PKA signaling modulation, cassiarins, alkaloids from Cassia siamea with potent antimalarial activity, bisindole alkaloids from Leuconotis species inducing autophagy through AKT-mTOR pathway inhibition, cyclolinopeptides from flaxseed suppressing osteoclast differentiation via the c-Fos/RANK axis, celogentins, bicyclic peptides from Celosia argentea inhibiting tubulin polymerization, and mollugin derivatives from Rubia species targeting TLR4-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. These studies demonstrate that tropical plant-derived natural products possess remarkable structural diversity and act on biologically relevant molecular targets. Furthermore, several cases illustrate the importance of mechanistic analysis and structural modification for the optimization of pharmacological activity. Collectively, this review highlights the significance of biodiversity-driven natural product exploration as a strategy for identifying functional seeds for future drug discovery.

papers.title: Shenkang injection ameliorates peritoneal fibrosis via the ESR1/PI3K/Akt pathway: Experimental verification and network pharmacology analysis.
papers.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
papers.authors: Huang W, Liu L, Ye Y, Huang A, Xu L, Qian Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Peritoneal fibrosis (PF) is the most distressing complication for peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients, leading to ultrafiltration failure and forcing discontinuation of PD. However, no effective treatment is currently available. Shenkang injection (SKI) is a traditional Chinese medicine which has shown anti-fibrosis efficacy. This study focused on the validation and preliminary prediction of the role and molecular mechanisms of SKI against PF.
The PF mouse model in vivo and cellular mesothelial-mesenchymal transition (MMT) model in vitro were conducted to verify whether SKI had mitigating fibrosis and anti-MMT effects. Mass spectrometry was used to collect and analyze the major compounds of SKI. Then we examine the potential targets and underlying mechanisms through network pharmacology analysis and molecular docking. Finally, in vitro experiments were performed to validate the function of SKI on signaling pathways.
The in vivo and in vitro experimental data showed that SKI alleviated the progression of PF. Further mass spectrometry and network pharmacology analysis revealed that the active compounds in SKI may bind to ESR1 and prevent its nuclear translocation, hence inhibiting the activation of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. Experimental validation of SKI inhibited high glucose (HG)-induced activation of the ESR1/PI3K/Akt pathway.
This study examines the therapeutic effect of SKI on PF and provides preliminary experimental support for further clinical investigation of SKI against PF.

papers.title: Preclinical Evidence and Mechanisms of Icariin on Bone Health in Ovariectomized Rodent Models of Osteoporosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Wang X, Zhou L, Shi T, Meng X, Li C, Liu X et al.
papers.abstract:
Osteoporosis, particularly postmenopausal osteoporosis, is a major global health concern, and current drugs often come with serious side effects. Herba Epimedii has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine to strengthen bones. Icariin, its principal flavonoid, has shown osteoprotective potential in preclinical studies, yet a comprehensive evaluation of its efficacy remains lacking.
To systematically evaluate the preclinical efficacy of icariin on bone density, microarchitecture, biomechanics, turnover markers, and its underlying mechanisms in ovariectomized (OVX) rodent models.
This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261366889). A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 16, 2026, to identify preclinical studies on icariin in OVX rodents. Effect sizes were pooled using random-effects models, and methodological quality was assessed using SYRCLE's Risk of Bias tool.
Twenty-six studies (708 animals) were included. Icariin significantly increased femoral BMD (SMD = 1.91, 95% CI: 1.36-2.46) and lumbar spine BMD (SMD = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.80-1.63). Trabecular microarchitecture improved substantially, with increased BV/TV (SMD = 3.24), Tb.Th (SMD = 2.90), Tb.N (SMD = 2.53), and decreased Tb.Sp (SMD = -3.06), all P < 0.001. Biomechanical strength was enhanced (femur maximum load: SMD = 2.87, P = 0.002). Serum ALP (SMD = -1.55, P = 0.002), OCN (SMD = -2.87, P = 0.02), and CTX-I (SMD = -2.29, P < 0.001) were significantly reduced; TRACP-5b reduction was significant only at >100 mg/kg (SMD = -1.34, P < 0.001). Mechanistically, icariin modulates OPG/RANKL, Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways.
This meta-analysis demonstrates that icariin effectively ameliorates OVX-induced bone loss in rodents, improving BMD, microarchitecture, biomechanics, and turnover markers through multiple pathways. These findings support icariin as a promising candidate for PMOP management, warranting clinical translation.

papers.title: Schisandra chinensis in sepsis intervention through multi-target mechanisms and organ protection.
papers.authors: Chen M, Wang H, Bu K, Zhang R, Qin C
papers.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by overwhelming inflammation, oxidative stress, immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive multiple organ injury. Schisandra chinensis (S. chinensis) and its bioactive constituents possess anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and organ-protective properties, but their sepsis-related evidence has not been comprehensively summarized. This narrative review critically summarizes the current evidence on S. chinensis and its bioactive constituents in sepsis, with emphasis on inflammatory regulation, immune homeostasis, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, regulated cell death, and sepsis-associated organ injury. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched without restriction on publication year, and the reference lists of relevant publications were also screened. Eligible studies were narratively synthesized according to intervention type, experimental model, biological effects, signaling pathways, and organ outcomes, with evidence from isolated or chemically characterized constituents distinguished from that derived from multicomponent preparations. Current evidence, derived predominantly from in vitro and LPS- or CLP-induced animal studies, indicates that S. chinensis constituents may attenuate inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, endothelial barrier disruption, and sepsis-associated lung and myocardial injury through the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB, JAK2/STAT3, NLRP3, Nrf2/GPX4, RhoA/ROCK1/MLC and MAPK pathways. However, clinical evidence remains limited and is mainly based on multicomponent traditional Chinese medicine preparations, preventing determination of the independent contribution of S. chinensis. Overall, S. chinensis is a promising but investigational adjunctive candidate for sepsis. Future studies should prioritize chemically standardized preparations, pharmacokinetic and safety characterization, causal validation of reproducible mechanisms, and biomarker-based identification of responsive sepsis phenotypes before early-phase and randomized clinical trials.

papers.title: Characterization and pharmacokinetic evaluation of natural composition self-assembled nanoemulsion.
papers.authors: Li J, Guan Q, Wang L, Cao L, Yan L, Zhu M et al.
papers.abstract: Nanophase is an effective drug delivery system. Self-assembling nanoemulsion (N-XY) was found in Xiaoyaosan; but its pharmacokinetics remain unclear.Objective: To explore the physicochemical properties, active components, release kinetics, and in vivo pharmacokinetic behavior of N-XY.Methods: Xiaoyaosan phase states were separated by centrifugal dialysis. N-XY was characterized using multiple analytical techniques, and active constituents against mammary gland hyperplasia were screened by HPLC fingerprinting combined with grey relational analysis (GRA). In vitro release was evaluated using dissolution studies, and in vivo pharmacokinetics were assessed in an animal model. In vitro-in vivo correlation (IVIVC) was established by linear regression analysis.Results:N-XY was isolated as a stable O/W nanoemulsion retaining key bioactive components. HPLC with GRA indicated nine components, including glycyrrhizic acid, contributed to anti-mammary hyperplasia effects. In vitro studies showed pH-responsive sustained release. Pharmacokinetics demonstrated prolonged in vivo retention and increased systemic exposure compared with A-XY, with significant IVIVC for the main bioactive components.Conclusion: N-XY is the primary bioactive phase of Xiaoyaosan, exhibiting intrinsic sustained-release and absorption-enhancing properties. This study not only elucidates the material basis and delivery characteristics of Xiaoyaosan but also provides a novel strategy for the rational development and identification of effective phases in traditional Chinese medicine formulas.

papers.title: Siddha Varmathadaval therapy in the management of stress-related insomnia: A case report.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.authors: Sakthivel K, Rajaiah MPSS
papers.abstract: Insomnia affects 10-30% of adults globally, with limited non-pharmacological options. This single-case report documents Siddha Varmathadaval therapy for stress-related insomnia. A 55-year-old woman presented with four-month history of insomnia (difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep) and daytime fatigue. Thookaminmai (insomnia) of Vatha-Pitham origin per Siddha principles was diagnosed. Baseline assessments showed severe insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index [ISI] = 21/28, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI] = 15/21, Athens Insomnia Scale [AIS] = 13/24, Perceived Stress Scale-10 [PSS-10] = 31/40). The patient underwent twenty-one consecutive daily Varmathadaval therapy sessions using Sukku Thailam (90-120 minutes each), administered by a trained Siddha physician. Post-therapy improvements included ISI = 8/28 (62% reduction), PSQI = 6/21 (60% reduction), AIS = 4/24 (69% reduction), and PSS-10 = 12/40 (61% reduction). Traditional Siddha parameters (Manikadai Nool, Neikuri) demonstrated progressive improvement correlating with clinical outcome. Sleep latency decreased (45 → 15 minutes) and total sleep time increased (4-5→6-7 hours). Benefits were sustained at 4-week (ISI = 9) and 12-week (ISI = 11) post-treatment follow-up, with mild stress-related variation. Varmathadaval therapy produced clinically significant, sustained improvements in stress-related insomnia. The therapy was safe and well-tolerated. Controlled trials with prospective stress assessment are warranted.

papers.title: Integrative Network Pharmacology, Molecular docking and Experimental Validation Uncover the Mechanism of Detoxifying Fumigation and Washing Granules against Hemorrhoids.
papers.authors: Chang Z, Shao X, Li Y, Zhang F, Zeng L, Li W et al.
papers.abstract:
Hemorrhoids significantly impair the quality of life of patients, primarily manifesting as pain, bleeding, and prolapse. Detoxifying fumigation and washing granules (DFWG), a traditional Chinese medicine, have demonstrated potential for alleviating hemorrhoids; however, its underlying mechanisms of action have yet to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the putative active constituents and possible mechanisms of DFWG in the treatment of hemorrhoids.
Active compounds in DFWG were identified through network pharmacology, and targets were screened using protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses were performed to identify core signaling pathways, and in vivo validation was conducted in a rat model of perianal edema.
Network pharmacology identified 328 active compounds and 1020 targets from DFWG, along with 314 hemorrhoid-related targets, yielding 46 overlapping targets. PPI analysis revealed 10 core targets, while GO and KEGG analyses indicated roles in regulating apoptosis and inflammation. Molecular docking results indicated that the binding energies between core target proteins and compounds were consistently below -5.0 kcal/mol. In vivo, DFWG reduced perianal swelling and rectoanal coefficient in model rats, lowered serum IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, and suppressed p-NF-κB p65/NF-κB p65 expression in perianal tissues.
The findings of network pharmacology indicate that DFWG primarily alleviates hemorrhoidal symptoms by modulating key inflammatory mediators. This mechanism is further supported by the observed reduction in inflammatory responses in model rats, along with concurrent improvements in pathological manifestations.
DFWG exerts protective effects against hemorrhoids in rats, likely by suppressing inflammation.

papers.title: Paris Saponins: A Comprehensive Review of Their Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Effects, and Mechanisms of Action.
papers.authors: Xie Q, Jiang JB, Huang D
papers.abstract: Paris polyphylla is a traditional medicinal plant widely used in Chinese and Indian medicine, and its steroidal saponins are regarded as the principal bioactive constituents responsible for many of its therapeutic effects. This review aims to provide an integrated overview of the chemical composition, nomenclature, pharmacological activities, molecular mechanisms, in vivo evidence, translational prospects, and safety of Paris saponins. Published evidence was narratively synthesized according to saponin structural features and sugar-chain composition, with particular attention to major monomers including Polyphyllin I, II, III, V, VI, VII, H, C, and G and to the standardization of their nomenclature. Evidence from cell-based, animal, and mechanistic studies was further organized to link individual saponins with their reported biological effects and molecular targets. Current evidence indicates that Paris saponins exhibit broad biological activities, including antitumor, antimicrobial, antiviral, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, hemostatic, immunomodulatory, organprotective, anthelmintic, and antioxidant effects. Mechanistically, these compounds regulate multiple molecular processes, including apoptosis, autophagy, cell-cycle progression, oxidative homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, immune responses, and tumor invasion and metastasis, through pathways such as PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK, NF-κB, and related signaling networks. Their pharmacological effects are strongly influenced by structural differences in steroidal aglycones, sugarchain composition, and glycosidic linkages. Although accumulating in vivo studies support their therapeutic potential, clinical translation remains constrained by hemolytic toxicity, limited bioavailability, complex metabolism, variable exposure-response relationships, and insufficient clinical evidence for structurally defined monomers. Overall, Paris saponins represent promising multitarget natural products, but future studies should integrate pharmacokinetics, toxicology, standardized nomenclature, structure-activity relationships, and well-designed clinical investigations to facilitate their safe and rational development.

papers.title: Advances in the Antidepressant Effects of Electroacupuncture Through Regulation of Microglia-Mediated BDNF Signaling and Hippocampal Neurogenesis.
papers.authors: Liu H, Wang J, Yang Q, Zhang Z, Peng Z, Lei X et al.
papers.abstract:
To summarize the regulatory network linking microglia, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) signaling, and hippocampal neurogenesis, and to clarify the potential antidepressant mechanisms of electroacupuncture.
We systematically reviewed and integrated recent findings from preclinical and clinical studies regarding microglial activation, BDNF/tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling, hippocampal neurogenesis, and electroacupuncture intervention in depressive disorders, retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI databases up to June 2026.
Depression is closely associated with neuroinflammation, impaired neuroplasticity, and disrupted hippocampal neurogenesis. Aberrant microglial activation may inhibit hippocampal neurogenesis by releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines, excessively engulfing synapses, and disturbing the neural microenvironment. These pathological changes interact with dysregulated BDNF/TrkB signaling and jointly contribute to depressive phenotypes. Electroacupuncture may exert antidepressant effects by modulating microglial phenotypic transformation, suppressing pro-inflammatory mediator release, and upregulating BDNF/TrkB signaling and its downstream pathways.
Electroacupuncture may improve depression through coordinated regulation of microglia-mediated neuroinflammation and BDNF-related neuroplasticity. This mechanism provides a scientific basis for further mechanistic research and clinical application of acupuncture in depression.

papers.title: Effect of Tai Chi Exercise on Fatigue in Renal Transplant Recipients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Qiao S, Liu C, Lu Y, Li H, Han W
papers.abstract:
Fatigue is a prevalent symptom in kidney transplant patients that not only affects quality of life but may also impact long-term graft survival. While Tai Chi has been shown to effectively reduce fatigue in patients with chronic diseases, research in kidney transplant recipients remains limited.
To explore the effects of Tai Chi exercise on fatigue among kidney transplant recipients and to investigate the effectiveness and safety of Tai Chi-based rehabilitation.
A prospective, single-center, parallel-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in Northeast China. The study period for patient recruitment and intervention implementation was from 1 June 2025, to 12 October 2025. Eligible participants were kidney transplant recipients aged 18-60 years who were at least 1 month post-transplantation. Sixty-four kidney transplant patients were randomly allocated (1:1) to the intervention group (Tai Chi exercise) or the control group (routine care only). The intervention group received a 12-week Tai Chi exercise program. The primary outcome was fatigue severity assessed at 12 weeks.
After 12 weeks of Tai Chi intervention, there were statistically significant differences in total fatigue scores between the two groups of renal transplant recipients. Sleep quality and 6-min walk distance were significantly improved.
Tai Chi exercise is a gentle and well-tolerated exercise intervention that can effectively improve fatigue in renal transplant recipients. Trial Registration: International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry: 2026000360.

papers.title: [Clinical evidence of acupuncture and moxibustion for depressive disorder: controversy, reflection and prospect].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang S, Wu Q, Ning B, Ma R, Wang C, Liang X et al.
papers.abstract: To clarify the clinical evidence required for integrating acupuncture and moxibustion treatment for depressive disorder into the mainstream psychiatric diagnostic and therapeutic system, as well as the existing deficiencies, this paper summarizes the current state of evidence for acupuncture and moxibustion treatment for depressive disorder from three perspectives: clinical guidelines, systematic reviews, and clinical trials. The differentiation of recommendations of different guidelines and its causes are analyzed, and the key issues such as the design and implementation of clinical research, efficacy evaluation, the integration of mechanisms with clinical practice, and the heterogeneity of acupuncture and moxibustion techniques and protocols are discussed. On this basis, the paper proposes that by conducting high-quality clinical research, constructing a multidimensional efficacy evaluation system, promoting the integration of mechanistic studies with clinical practice, and strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration and the translation of research outcomes, the therapeutic characteristics, target populations, and clinical value of acupuncture and moxibustion treatment for depressive disorder can be further clarified. This will provide a reference for improving the relevant clinical evidence system and promoting standardized application.

papers.title: [Development and application of a fumigation moxibustion device for small animals].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang W, Zhang X, Geng J, Sun Y, Wu S, Zhou M et al.
papers.abstract: A localized and quantitative fumigation moxibustion device for small animals was developed. The device consists of four components: an outer shell, a fumigation moxibustion chamber, fixing component, and adhesive component. It provides accurate positioning and stable moxibustion distance, enables real-time observation of the burning status and progress of moxa sticks, accommodates moxa sticks with different diameters, and has the advantages of convenient operation and high safety. However, the device is mainly applicable to acupoints on the head, face and back of laboratory animals, while its application to abdominal acupoints remains limited due to issues such as smoke backflow and difficulty in attachment.

papers.title: [Textual research on the origin and development of Xi-cleft point theory].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Liu S, Li R, Wu H, Qiu W, Wang T, Song Z et al.
papers.abstract: Xi-cleft point redefines the practical connotation of acupoint theory based on terminological system within the classical acupuncture framework. Xi-cleft point was proposed in Huangdi Mingtang Jing (The Yellow Emperor's Acupoints Canon of Mingtang), and was primarily intended to re-categorize the acupoints below the elbows and knees that were newly introduced beyond those recorded in Huangdi Neijing (The Yellow Emperor's Internal Classic) despite lacking clearly shared therapeutic indications in practice. But, the common therapeutic indications of this supplemented Xi-cleft points are unclear. The current theory of Xi-cleft point, "Xi-cleft points treat acute diseases", was summarized by Japanese acupuncture practitioners, and was introduced to China with the publication of corresponding Chinese translations of Japanese books of acupuncture and moxibustion. Later in 1984, YANG Jiasan edited Shuxue Xue (Science of Acupoints) and determined the indications of this special point, "Xi-cleft points of yin meridians treat blood disorders, while those of yang meridians treat pain". The common therapeutic indications of Xi-cleft points were analogically generalized by Chinese and Japanese medical scholars in the modern times based on the practical experience with some Xi-cleft points. In the time of Huangdi Mingtang Jing, Xi-cleft point was proposed to improve the theoretical framework of acupoint theory. Since there is lack of the anatomical distribution characteristics among Xi-cleft points regarding to the correspondence of the body to nature and similar indications, these Xi-cleft points do not necessarily share common therapeutic indications. Therefore, it needs to be validated in practice to identify whether the therapeutic characteristics of one specific Xi-cleft point are consistent with the current theory of Xi-cleft point, rather than regard it with the specific indication of the acupoint itself.
